audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid opens 'Shield of Durand's magic damage reduction is wasted here — Zac is a sustain tank, not a burst assassin you can sponge into a free kill', and the full tldr and report[0] both open 'Respect the physical damage'.
audit.why: Unstable Matter is explicitly 'a percentage of their maximum health as magic damage', and it is Zac's primary trade tool on a 5-second cooldown. Shield of Durand reduces magic 25/30/35/40/45% against physical's 12.5/15/17.5/20/22.5%, so the stance is at its most effective against exactly the button Zac spams — the opposite of what the page says twice. Telling a Galio his defensive cooldown is dead weight in the one lane where it is doubly effective is the most costly single error in this entry.
audit.corrected: Unstable Matter is magic damage, so Shield of Durand cuts it at double the rate it cuts physical — 25% at rank 1 rising to 45%. Charge the stance into his percent-health AoE, do not save it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (W Unstable Matter: 'dealing a percentage of their maximum health as magic damage', cooldown 5, range 350)

audit.whatIsWrong: The prose and the chart on this page contradict each other and both contradict the already-audited mirror. content.win reads Galio, Galio, Galio, Skill, Galio, Skill, Zac while whys[0..3] say 'Zac's passive blob heals ignore your single-ability poke', 'his early Unstable Matter plus Stretching Strike CC beat your mana-hungry kit at 2-3', 'his even trades plus blob heals keep it a coinflip, not a win for you', and 'his sustained percent-HP trades... shove you off the wave'. spikes[0] and early say the same.
audit.why: audits/top/zac__galio.json has already been written and aligned Zac's full layer to Galio, Galio, Galio, Galio, Galio, Skill, Zac — Galio through Level 6, shared at first item, Zac at two-plus. Zac's own packet has him at 48.26% over 230 games, a losing lane for him. The Galio-side prose is the only thing in either direction still saying Zac wins the early game, and it also disagrees with the chart printed directly above it.
audit.corrected: Galio, Galio, Galio, Galio, Galio, Skill, Zac, with the level 1-5 why-lines rewritten to explain why Galio wins them instead of why he loses them.
sources: scratchpad packet galio.json entry zac (43.75%, 32 games) and zac's packet (48.26%, 230 games)

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one cooldown appears anywhere. breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0], report[5], tldr and winCon all say 'when Elastic Slingshot is down' without the number, and the passive revive is described as 'blob heals' with no timer.
audit.why: Elastic Slingshot is 21/18/15/12/9 — twenty-one seconds at rank 1 is a genuinely long engage cooldown and it is the number that makes 'punish the downtime' real advice. Unstable Matter is a flat 5s, which is why extended trades bleed you. Stretching Strikes is 14s at rank 1 and Let's Bounce is 120s. Cell Division's revive is on a five-minute cooldown, which is the difference between a kill that sticks and one that does not.
audit.corrected: Elastic Slingshot 21s at rank 1 — that is your window. Unstable Matter a flat 5s. Stretching Strikes 14s. Let's Bounce 120s. Cell Division's revive is a five-minute cooldown, so check whether it is already spent before you commit a kill.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (E 21/18/15/12/9; W 5; Q 14/12.5/11/9.5/8; R 120/105/90; P Cell Division 'has a 5 minute cooldown')

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing mentions that Justice Punch begins with a backward step, and nothing says it answers Stretching Strikes.
audit.why: Riot's text is 'Galio will briefly step back and charge, knocking up the first enemy champion he encounters.' The backstep moves him out of the spot an 800-range Stretching Strikes was aimed at, so pressing E as the arm comes out both dodges the grab and answers with a knockup. The mirror entry already documents this from Zac's side, so it needs to read the same way here.
audit.corrected: Justice Punch steps back before it charges, so pressing it as his Stretching Strikes arm comes out can dodge the grab and knock him up in the same motion.
sources: champ-data/_kits/galio.json (E Justice Punch: 'briefly step back and charge')
champ-data/_kits/zac.json (Q Stretching Strikes range 800, flags projectile)
audits/top/zac__galio.json (same interaction, stated from Zac's side)

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[2] says to save the taunt and knockup to interrupt Elastic Slingshot, but the mechanism and the cooldown are never given.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags 'enemy-dash-deniable: Your Justice Punch (E) shuts off Zac's Elastic Slingshot (E) — hold it for the engage, not the poke.' Elastic Slingshot is a 21-second charged launch at rank 1; spending your 11-second knockup on it is a strictly winning trade of cooldowns, and that arithmetic is what makes the advice stick.
audit.corrected: Justice Punch is 11s and Elastic Slingshot is 21s at rank 1 — trading your knockup for his launch wins the cooldown exchange every time.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[2].why says 'the dash is interruptible and root-able mid-flight'.
audit.why: Justice Punch cannot be interrupted once it is travelling, and Zac has no root — his crowd control is the Stretching Strikes throw, the Elastic Slingshot landing knockup and the Let's Bounce knockups. Naming a root he does not have replaces the displacement he does.
audit.corrected: Zac has no root. Justice Punch cannot be interrupted mid-travel; what beats it is his Elastic Slingshot landing, so spend the punch on his launch rather than into it.
sources: wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Galio (Justice Punch cannot be interrupted mid-travel)

audit.why: report Itemization already carries 'Oblivion Orb early — his healing fights your trade math', which is right: _missing-interactions.json flags needs-antiheal on Cell Division, and the passive both heals off reabsorbed chunks and revives him. The content layer does not mention it, which is why the fix lands there.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (P Cell Division flags heal, percentHealth)

audit.why: The packet flags 'Stretching Strike', "Zac's Elastic Slingshot" and "Shield of Durand's" as probable wrong ability names. 'Stretching Strike' is genuinely wrong — the ability is Stretching Strikes, plural — and my spikes[0] rewrite drops that phrasing; the other two are false positives.

43.75% over 32 games on this side against 48.26% over 230 on Zac's side — the two samples do not reconcile exactly, but both are near even and EVEN at 6/10 is a fair label. I did not change the rating on 32 games; I aligned the stage chart to the mirror, which is the larger sample.

edits.before: Zac out-bodies you at Levels 1-3 — his passive blob heals let him shrug off your single-ability Q poke, and once he has Unstable Matter (W) his percent-HP AoE plus Stretching Strike (Q) CC out-trade anything you have before your full combo. Don't throw a greedy Q hoping to chunk him; he walks up, eats the magic with his HP pool, and refunds it by stepping on a blob. Last-hit with the tip of Q and wait for your Q-W-E at 3 just to stabilize, because his sustain turns every isolated poke into a wash.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are yours if you play the range. Winds of War reaches 825 against an 800 Stretching Strikes, so chip from outside the grab and refuse the melee war his blobs would refund. From 2, Unstable Matter is percent-health MAGIC damage on a flat 5-second cooldown, which is exactly what Shield of Durand is best at — charge the stance and trade into it rather than saving it. At 3, remember Justice Punch steps back before it charges: pressing it as his arm comes out dodges the grab and knocks him up.

edits.before: Shield of Durand's magic damage reduction is wasted here — Zac is a sustain tank, not a burst assassin you can sponge into a free kill, so the W-taunt-into-E-knockup punish that blanks AP threats never converts into a kill on him. Hold W and E to interrupt his Elastic Slingshot engage instead of opening trades you lose. The lane is really about Level 6: Hero's Entrance is your spike not because you beat Zac, but because you can flag a winning lane globally and make the rest of the map matter.
edits.after: Shield of Durand is not wasted here — Unstable Matter is magic damage, and the stance cuts magic at double the rate it cuts physical, so charging into his percent-health AoE is the right trade. Spend Justice Punch on Elastic Slingshot: yours is 11 seconds and his is 21 at rank 1, so you win that exchange every time. The lane is still about Level 6 — Hero's Entrance flags a winning lane globally — but buy Grievous Wounds, because his blobs and his 5-minute revive refund everything.

notes: Mirror alignment: audits/top/zac__galio.json was already written and set the chart to Galio, Galio, Galio, Galio, Galio, Skill, Zac; I matched it and rewrote the Galio-side why-lines, which were the only text in either direction still claiming Zac wins the early game. The two packets also disagree on the win rate for this pairing — galio's packet says 43.75% over 32 games, zac's says 48.26% over 230 — so a Galio reading his page and a Zac reading his will see numbers that do not sum to 100. Worth reconciling upstream. KIT FLAG WARNING: zac.json tags Elastic Slingshot with 'grounding', and _missing-interactions.json builds a 'dash-denied: Zac can deny your mobility (Justice Punch) with Elastic Slingshot' rule on top of it. Riot's text is 'Zac attaches his arms to the ground and stretches back, launching himself forward' — that is Zac anchoring himself, not applying Grounded to an enemy, so the flag looks like a parse misfire on the word 'ground' and I did not write that interaction into the page. Galio facts verified at wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Galio: Shield of Durand cuts magic 25/30/35/40/45% and physical exactly half; Justice Punch knocks up 0.75s, cannot be interrupted mid-travel, is disabled while Grounded, halts on terrain or champions; Winds of War 825; Hero's Entrance channels 2.75s, CC-immune after 1.25s; Colossal Smash is a 5s empowered auto scaling with 60% bonus MR. Galio's own kit file tags E 'terrain' and omits 'knockup' — both wrong against Riot's description.
